graphEvents.label: OpenBot skills model: three origins and one review gate
LearningProposal is a reviewable staging record with add/update/remove

label: A skill record is slug, title, summary, instructions, tools, ownerId, botIds, usableOnYourBots; the slug is both the / command and the address.
A skill's tools list is declarative, not a grant: naming an action gives no bot access to it, so approving a skill cannot widen a bot's reach.
Skill ownership is three-valued in one record: ownerId (person or null for the organization), botIds (bots that offer it), usableOnYourBots (whether the caller may attach it).
Skill visibility is computed per caller from ownership and team grants, not stored per viewer.
The three skill origins are written, recorded from a demonstration, and proposed from conversations.

The proposed-from-use origin is a first-class reviewable object: LearningProposal carries runId, operation add|update|remove, status pending_review|approved|rejected, reason, reviewedAt and publishedSkillId.
Approval is what publishes: publishedSkillId is null until approved, and operation remove lets the same pipeline retire a skill.
A proposal must be readable before it is judged: the review shows its SKILL.md, why it was proposed, and the conversations and recordings behind it.
Skill delivery is a per-run snapshot, so a run's skills are fixed when the run starts.
Learned guidance never grants tools or replaces manually authored skills.
Skill precedence on a run is bot's own, then the person's own, then skills another person opened; same-named skills from two people are both kept as container/name.
Sharing is a per-person three-way choice (own bots by default, every bot, or skills opened one by one) and an admin must allow the wider choice first.
The sharing index is in memory, re-read at once on the saving replica and within 30 seconds elsewhere; a missing or refusing person container never fails a run.
Skilled bots has no per-bot skill record: BOT.md has no skills field, so a bot's skills are whatever the shared skill system discovers.

direction: Treating a skill's tools list as a capability grant
reason: The schema says naming an action gives no bot access to it, so no grant check is needed at approval time.

direction: Modelling the three skill origins as three storage locations
reason: All three produce the same Skill record; only the proposal path adds a staging row.
